question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session messaging now, and what peer identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, delivery, and transcript-ownership contract must it use?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses Gateway, session-state, message-delivery, config, and credential boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security model.

options.title: Design the contract first
options.body: Use this issue as the concrete session-tool tracker while aligning it with peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and the broader federation FRD before merging code.

options.title: Advance the linked narrow PR
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43656 proceed only after conflicts, security review, upgrade behavior, and real multi-gateway proof are resolved.

options.title: Defer native core support
options.body: Document plugin, MCP, channel, or operator-run workarounds only if maintainers intentionally decide not to add core cross-gateway session routing now.

recommendation.title: Design the contract first
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the concrete session-tool tracker while aligning it with peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, transcript ownership, and the broader federation FRD before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans sessions_spawn, Gateway role policy, and Gateway client/protocol surfaces that frame the trust-boundary choice.
